title: Cross-Category Data Comparison
tagline: Year 3 — Combining different kinds of data about the same items: populations, rates, incomes and areas

introduction.overview: A cross-category table lists several kinds of data about the same items, such as population, literacy rate, income per head and area for several states. Questions combine categories: literate people = population × literacy rate; density = population ÷ area; total income = population × income per head. The key is to know what each combination means and to keep units straight, so that million × thousand is billion.
introduction.placementRelevance: Cross-category comparison sets are standard in DI sections of company and bank tests.
introduction.realWorldContext: Comparing regions on several indicators for planning and investment uses these combinations.

learningObjectives: Combine counts and rates to get new counts
Compute weighted averages for the group

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Rate × base = count. Total ÷ count = average. Units multiply: million × thousand = billion.

coreDefinitions: Category: one kind of data (population, income).
Derived measure: a new number built from two categories.
Weighted average: total of values ÷ total of weights.
Unit consistency: using compatible units before combining.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Each state is a record. A cross-category question builds a new field from two old ones.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Name the new quantity, write its formula in terms of the categories, check the units, and compute it for each state if needed.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Density
importantRulesAndFormulas.description: Units: million ÷ thousand sq km = thousand per sq km.

mainNarrative: Literate populations (million): S1 60, S2 49.2, S3 81.6, S4 36, S5 78. S3 has the most literate people even though its literacy rate is among the lowest, because its population is largest.
Density in persons per sq km: population (million) × 1,000 ÷ area (thousand sq km). S1 400, S2 600, S3 375, S4 500, S5 800. S5 is the most densely populated.
Total income (₹ billion) = population × per-capita income: S1 4,800, S2 5,400, S3 5,400, S4 4,400, S5 7,000. S5 has the highest total income although S4 has the highest income per head.
The group literacy rate is total literate ÷ total population = 304.8 ÷ 400 = 76.2%, not the average of the five rates (78.6%).
The weighted average income per head is 27,000 ÷ 400 = ₹67.5 thousand.

deepDiveAspects.title: Rate vs count
deepDiveAspects.content: A high rate with a small base can give a smaller count than a lower rate with a large base.

deepDiveAspects.title: Weighted averages
deepDiveAspects.content: To combine rates, weight by the base: literacy by population, income per head by population.

solvedExamples.title: Count from a rate
solvedExamples.question: State S2 has a population of 60 million with 82% literacy. How many literate people does it have?

solvedExamples.title: Density
solvedExamples.question: State S5 has 100 million people in 125 thousand sq km. What is its density (persons per sq km)?

solvedExamples.title: Group rate
solvedExamples.question: Five states have 304.8 million literate people among 400 million. What is the group literacy rate?
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Not the average of the five rates.

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Decide which two categories combine and how (rate × base, total ÷ area, population × income) and keep the units straight.

commonMistakes.mistake: Mixing a rate with a count

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: A literate count must be below the population.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Add derived columns to the table once.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Many questions need only one derived column.
